Consider the Boolean operator with the following properties:
[latex]x \# 0=x, x \# 1=\bar{x}[/latex], [latex]x \# x=0[/latex] and [latex]x \# \bar{x}=1[/latex]. Then [latex]x \# y[/latex] is equivalent to
questions.solution:
[latex]x\#0=x[/latex], [latex]x\#1=\bar x[/latex], [latex]x\#x=0[/latex], [latex]x\#\bar x=1[/latex]: these are exactly the properties of XOR.

[latex]x\#y=x\bar y+\bar xy[/latex]

Answer: [latex]x\bar y+\bar xy[/latex]

questions.text: The 16 bit 2's complement representation of an integer is 1111 1111 1111 0101;   its decimal representation is__________ .
questions.solution:
The MSB is 1, so the number is negative. Take the 2's complement of 1111 1111 1111 0101:
invert [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0000 0000 0000 1010, add 1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0000 0000 0000 1011 = 11.

Answer: -11

questions.text: We want to design a synchronous counter that counts these quence 0-1-0-2-0-3 and then repeats. The minimum number of J-K flip flop srequired to implement this counteris ________.
questions.solution:
The sequence 0, 1, 0, 2, 0, 3 has 6 steps, and the three 0s are followed by different numbers, so the counter needs 6 different internal states.

6 states need [latex]\lceil\log_2 6\rceil=3[/latex] flip-flops (the output is then decoded from the state).

Answer: 3

questions.text: A processor can support a maximum memory of 4GB, where the memory is word-addressable (a word consists of two bytes). The size of the address bus of the process or is at least bits________.
questions.solution:
4 GB = [latex]2^{32}[/latex] bytes. One word = 2 bytes, so there are [latex]2^{31}[/latex] words.
Word addressable [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] [latex]2^{31}[/latex] addresses [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 31 address bits.

Answer: 31

questions.text: A queue is implemented using an array such that ENQUEUE and DEQUEUE operations are performed efficiently. Which one of the following statements is CORRECT (n refers to the number of items in the queue)?
questions.solution:
Use a circular array with front and rear indices: ENQUEUE writes at rear and moves it, DEQUEUE reads at front and moves it (both modulo the array size). No shifting is needed, so both are [latex]O(1)[/latex].

Answer: Both operations can be performed in O(1) time
